newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russians plan new Mir docking attempt on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Russians plan new Mir docking attempt on Monday.

text.p: Russian officials plan to try again on Monday to redock a cargo craft with the damaged Mir space station after a computer error delayed the first attempt on Sunday, a Mission Control duty officer said.
He said by telephone the second attempt was due to take place at 4.57 p.m. (1257 GMT).

Mir crew and Mission Control suddenly delayed a planned redocking of the seven-metre (23 feet) long Progress craft with the space station on Sunday because of a computer programming error which arose only three hours earlier, officials said.

The delay was the latest in a series of setbacks that have seen Russia's orbiting space station lurch from crisis to crisis, and raised the possibility of another delay in vital repairs planned for Wednesday.

The redocking manoeuvre is a repeat of a procedure carried out on June 25, when a different Progress vehicle docking with Mir collided with the station's Spektr module, causing a major loss of power in the worst accident in Mir's 11-year history.

The Russian cosmonauts who will make the Spektr repairs, commander Anatoly Solovyov and flight engineer Pavel Vinogradov, had planned a dress rehearsal on Monday wearing spacesuits. It was not immediately clear whether this would go ahead.
Progress delivered oxygen, food, water and tools to Mir on July 7 and is now filled mostly with garbage.
Redocking a rubbish-filled module will provide better balance for Mir and will protect its hatch from prolonged solar exposure.
Progress undocked on August 6 to make room for a Soyuz spaceship bringing Solovyov and Vinogradov from Earth.
